request.input: So, based on what you told me, I should contact my pharmacy or doctor immediately to get an emergency bridge supply of Zoloft. Is that correct?

content.text:
**Yes, that is correct.**

If you are currently experiencing withdrawal symptoms, the fastest and most effective way to stop the pain and stabilize your mood is to get back on your medication as soon as possible.

**Here is exactly what to do:**

1.  **Call your pharmacy first.** Tell them: *"I have run out of my Zoloft prescription and I am experiencing withdrawal symptoms. Is it possible to get a 3-day emergency bridge supply until my doctor can renew the prescription on Monday?"*
2.  **If the pharmacy says no, call your doctor’s office.** Even if it is the weekend, there is usually an "on-call" physician or a nursing line. Tell them you are out of medication and experiencing discontinuation syndrome. They can often send an electronic prescription to a 24-hour pharmacy immediately.

**Why do this now?**
Zoloft has a relatively short half-life compared to some other antidepressants, meaning it leaves your system quickly. The longer you go without it, the more intense the "brain zaps" and emotional instability become. Getting a few pills today or tomorrow will stop the downward spiral and make your workday on Monday significantly easier.

**Go make those calls now.** You don't have to suffer through the weekend if there is a way to get your meds sooner.
